text:
maria: Quick check-in on the observability envelope proposal. New angle: lean header + pointer-first payload to control cardinality, plus an ingest-side dedupe window for identical events. Want to align on billing precedence and migration story.
sam: short version: header contains only routing/cost keys (service, env, cost_key, dedupe_key) and a payload pointer (s3/kv/ref). full attributes live off-index.
maria: exactly. example header shape: `{"env":"prod","service":"ingest","cost_key":"acct:acme-42","dedupe_key":"d12345","payload_ref":"kv://p/abc"}`. keep it tiny.
lekha: +1 but we need explicit rules for "cost_key" precedence. propose resolution order: 1) cost_key (header) 2) billing_hint (header minimal) 3) legacy trace->billing lookup (compat layer). Document as deterministic precedence so queries are stable.
devon: how do we prevent double-charging when both a trace and a metric envelope exist for the same operation? dedupe_key + origin_type + ingest-window should handle it: if two envelopes share dedupe_key within 5s and same cost_key, collapse to single charge. we'll store dedupe metadata in an ephemeral de-dup table for the window.
sam: feasible but we must bound memory. 5s sounds ok for typical latency. ops: can we async compact after ingest and emit a canonical indexed doc that downstream billing uses?
lekha: yes: ingest -> canonicalizer job that merges same dedupe_key within window and writes a canonical index doc with chosen cost_key. canonical doc kept for 90d. original envelopes archived but not indexed in billing store.
natalie: product asks: how will this affect SLA for chargeback queries? we need canonical docs available within 1m of ingest for near-realtime dashboards.
maria: target: canonicalizer completes within 30s for 95% of cases. fallback: query layer will consult ephemeral de-dup table during canary if canonical doc missing.
devon: enrichment story: pointer-first requires an enrich-hint id (short) in header so enrichers can attach attributes later. If enrichment fails within TTL, canonicalizer must still pick billing_hint fallback. propose enrich TTL=48h for non-critical attrs, but billing_hint must be present at ingest.
lekha: TTL ops burden scales with tenant count. recommend two-tier TTL: 1) billing_hint (immediate) 2) enrich_lookup (48h but limited to flagged tenants). default keep TTL 24h to reduce memory.
sam: query compatibility: we'll ship a tiny compatibility microservice that exposes /v1/legacy-billing-map and resolves trace_id->cost_key for old dashboards. This avoids immediate rewrites. It's temporary (6mo).
maria: migration plan (high-level): 1) Gateway enforces header schema (reject >6 keys) 2) Deploy pointer-first ingest flag behind feature flag 3) Enable dedupe-window canonicalizer in canary 4) Run mapping service for legacy queries 5) Backfill canonical docs for 90d.
ci-bot: note: integration test "envelope-schema-gate" failing on branch feature/envelope-compact (see CI details link).
lekha: ops: we also need ingress limits: gzip required, max header size 512 bytes, warn on payload_ref size > 128. Also metric to surface top offending tenants so we can consult them during rollout.
devon: storage/cost regression plan: during canary we collect: ingest-rows, canonicalized-rows, payload-archive-size, per-tenant delta. make this visible to finance and SRE.
natalie: please include an "expected delta" estimate in the RFC for small/medium/large tenants (ballpark numbers) and make canary gates budget-based. if projected delta > 5% for a tenant, auto-exclude from next canary wave until we consult them.
maria: agreed. canary gating rules: start 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. at each step compare actual delta to expected; rollback if >10% unexpected delta or >0.5% error-rate bump.
sam: edge-case: partial duplicates where dedupe_key differs slightly. canonicalizer heuristics should prefer newest envelope unless explicit origin_priority tag exists (e.g., billing source "billing.pipeline" > "debug.logs"). define origin_priority table.
lekha: operational note: we must ensure dedupe table is sharded by cost_key to avoid hot keys. also TTL flush must be atomic enough to avoid double canonical writes.
devon: for auditability, keep raw envelopes in cold storage for 365d. canonical docs in hot index 90d, legacy mapping 540d.
maria: action items: I'll draft RFC v2 with canonical header schema, dedupe window semantics, canonicalizer contract, migration checklist, and canary gating metrics. Owners: @sam, @lekha, @devon for sections.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-envelopes -> 2026-04-02 03:30 UTC (automated).
natalie: please include a demo dashboard in Console for the canary showing per-tenant delta and top cardinality contributors.
maria: will do. meeting follow-up: 30m next Tue to go through RFC and expected numbers. thanks everyone.
